He also provided a brief update on his and VP Abby Benson’s efforts to ‘undo’ the state-imposed cap on FTE’s at URI, which has been in place for far too long.

ii. Call for Nominations: At the October Faculty Senate meeting, Sens. Kendall Moore, William Krieger, and Alison Roberts were chosen as this year’s Nominating Committee. Per Section 5.2 of the Senate By-Laws, the Nominating Committee shall prepare a slate of candidates for one (1) one-year and two (2) two-year vacancies on the Executive Committee. The Executive Committee Election shall be held May 7, 2026. Please reach out to a member of the Nominating Committee if you are interested in this role.

VP Preisser encouraged faculty to spread the word, and suggested that they explore relevant housing webpages or reach out to him directly for more information.

Budget and Administration Committee Annual Report - Chair Triki explained that his committee’s primary task this year has been to try to measure faculty sentiment toward the new budget mode via a survey distributed broadly to the community.

Chair Triki agreed that the survey probably did roll out at an unfortunate time for measuring faculty understanding and satisfaction.
He noted that one positive takeaway from the results was the degree to which faculty are engaged and paying attention, and he praised their resilience in the face of unrelenting bad news.

Introduction to digital photojournalism and editing. Emphasis on visual reporting techniques and ethics. Required projects, lab work, readings, discussions. (Studio) Pre: JOR220 COLLEGE OF BUSINESS BAI100 | Preparation for BAI109, effective Winter 2027 (0 crs.) Course serves as a foundational bridge designed to prepare students for the business quantitative sequence. Aimed at reinforcing key concepts, the course focuses on strengthening skills in areas critical for BAI109 success. (Online) Pre: Permission of instructor. S/U Only. FIN222 | Introduction to Financial Planning, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) This course provides a foundational overview of the financial planning process, serving as both a practical guide for personal financial management and an introduction to the Financial Planning profession. Students will explore key concepts, including the time value of money, cash flow management, tax strategies, risk management (insurance), investment principles, and retirement planning. By the end of the course, students will be able to construct a basic financial plan and understand the ethical responsibilities of financial advisors. (Lec. 3)
